checks.note: Food is a settlement-existential; monthsOfFood < 1 means the buffer is nearly gone regardless of phase.

orders.note: Frees Unity and worker capacity (bottlenecks.md crisis step 1). ResearchStopCmd takes no args in the catalogue.
Stop the clock while the human assesses; unpausing is a human decision.

orders.step: In the UI: (1) pause all non-essential production (ToggleEnabledCmd per machine may be prepared by the agent instead, entity-settings, confirm); (2) divert iron to mechanical parts to feed the maintenance depot; (3) Unity-boost the maintenance depot (manual only — no catalogue command spends Unity, format G5); (4) confirm diesel generators sit on the OUTPUT side of fuel storage so a fuel hiccup cannot kill power.
orders.why: bottlenecks.md crisis response steps 2-4; several levers have no command-channel equivalent.

crisis_protocol.trigger_note: The death-spiral trio (fuel, maintenance, electricity) from bottlenecks.md: lose one and everything cascades. Crisis beats plan — phase progression suspends while this runs.

invariants.note: Armed from t0 per the starting-diesel assumption above; phase 0 verifies the assumption before first unpause.

checks.note: Fires only if the starting-diesel assumption is wrong at t0; after phase 4 the same signal is a real fuel crisis and phase checks take over.

phases.intent: Pause, look, verify the plan's hypotheses against the actual save, pin the vital products, and queue nothing yet. No building happens in this phase; it exists so every later gate reads observed state, not the layout-policy hypotheses.
phases.name: Scout & bootstrap

orders.note: Starter phase 1 opens with 'pause, scout'. Verified command.

orders.step: Open the Layers view (resource overlays) and record: oil patch bearing/distance from the comms station, coal deposit, limestone, iron deposit distance, coastline and shipyard position to the south. Use the terrain inspector (Shift+L) on candidate mine spots to see ore layers. Do NOT place anything yet.
orders.why: layout-policy.md: starting-area details are a reported hypothesis; verify against the actual save before any tile-level placement.

orders.observe: Record the opening snapshot: Product_Diesel / Product_IronScrap / Product_ConcreteSlab / Product_Copper quantities; population and housing from bridge status; researchedCount baseline (needed for research.completed observation, format G1). Compare against the plan assumptions and report every mismatch to the human. If Product_Diesel == 0, STOP: the globals diesel invariant must be amended by a human before unpausing.

orders.step: Claim any tutorial-goal freebies the game offers.

orders.note: Pin the death-spiral vitals so they are visible on the HUD from hour one. Repeat this order shape for Product_IronScrap and Product_ConstructionParts once unlocked (ConstructionParts may not be unlocked at t0 — its product.unlocked precondition will simply hold the order until phase 2).

checks.note: Scrap is finite: below this, phase 3 (mining) stops being optional. Threshold is a plan-set target.

phases.intent: Consume the comms-station scrap pile in a DISPOSABLE starter cluster: scrap smelter (1 blast furnace + 2 casters), wood-burning coal maker, diesel generator, two research labs, tree-clearing designations, controlled ocean dumping. Start the research queue. Nothing built here is permanent (layout policy).
phases.name: Scrap-fed starter cluster

orders.note: Research order #1 (research-order.md): unlocks assemblies, Construction Parts I, Mechanical Parts, Electronics I. Id SOURCED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): shipped proto registration Start("Construction", Ids.Research.CpPacking) in Mafi.Base (ConstructionResearchData) with exactly these unlocks; the string ResearchCpPacking appears in Philip's live bridge researched list. The tree calls it a starting tech — it may already be complete at t0, in which case this order is skipped by its verify. (The old candidate ResearchCp1Production is a goal id, not a research node — see the plan-level assumption.)

orders.step: Queue the first-15 research list (research-order.md) up front in the research UI, in the order the phases below consume it: Construction (ResearchCpPacking); Maintenance (listed as 'Power & Maintenance' in older guides; ResearchPowerAndMaintenance); Trading Dock (ResearchTradeDock); Vehicles & Mining (ResearchVehicleAndMining); Beacon; Tools; Advanced concrete (the wiki's 'Concrete Production'; ResearchConcreteAdvanced); Basic Diesel; Synthetic Rubber (ResearchRubberProduction); Copper Refinement; Construction II (ResearchCp2Packing); Conveyor Belts; Ship Dock Repair; Groundwater Pump; Fuel Station. All ids sourced 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0). Two labs keep research ahead of building.
orders.why: The per-node ResearchQueueDequeueCmd orders live in their consuming phases (so gates stay honest); this step is the starter skill's queue-up-front instruction. It stays a human step (bulk queueing in the UI is one pass), but since plan v1.3.0 every id in the list is sourced — the eyeball-against-the-screen rationale is retired.

orders.note: Degrades to a manual build from layout-policy.md's temporary list: first scrap smelter (1 blast furnace + 2 casters on scrap), wood-burning coal maker, diesel generator placed on the OUTPUT side of fuel storage, two research labs. Starter cluster is disposable — build cheap, near the comms station/docks, never anchor a permanent build here. Placement route (v1.2.2): the smelter core (pack slug iron-v1) goes through the companion /place flow — human confirm, QoSBuilder job; the coal maker, generator and labs are single-building manual placements (no pack asset contains them — plans-blueprint-status.md ref #1).

orders.step: Designate tree clearing around the starter cluster, and set controlled ocean waste dumping on the 'flat' setting in a zone AWAY from the ship's docking spot (dumping extends coastline into future building land; keep the south/east coastline stretch reserved for the future big harbour — do not build or dump on it).
orders.why: Starter phase 1 + layout policy rules 2 and 4.

orders.note: Scout is done: run at speed 1 while the starter cluster goes up (a human unpauses — SetSimPauseStateCmd {isPaused: false} — as the companion order to this one; both are verified sim-control commands, confirm class in this plan).

orders.observe: Watch the research queue: Power & Maintenance is order #2 in this plan (maintenance-before-anything-else). The source skill flags an order variant — some guides take it after Trading Dock. The variant is recorded here, not silently resolved.

checks.note: Construction-parts starvation (bottlenecks.md): do not overbuild fabrication to compensate — 'don't rush' is the source's explicit warning; report and let the human decide.

Maintenance has no product id and no stock route (format G6) — a broad NotEnoughInput share across machines is the observable proxy for the maintenance/power legs of the death-spiral trio. Crude by design; the companion detectors refine it.

exit_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: Construction researched → ~4 manual assemblies near the smelter (construction parts priority 1, then mechanical parts, then electronics), maintenance depot online, one farm near the settlement. This is the power+maintenance stability phase: maintenance must never stall from here on.
phases.name: Assembly + power & maintenance stability

orders.note: Research order #2. Id CONFIRMED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): shipped proto registration Start("Maintenance", Ids.Research.PowerAndMaintenance) in Mafi.Base (unlocks MaintenanceDepotT0), and ResearchPowerAndMaintenance appears in Philip's live bridge researched list. The flagged ambiguity is retired: ResearchPowerMaintenance is not a research node in the shipped data (no proto registration, no Ids field) — it reached research_ids.txt via the mixed goal/other id dump. Note the node's shipped display name is 'Maintenance'; 'Power & Maintenance' is the older guides' name.

Manual build until authored: ~4 manual assemblies near the smelter. Recipe priority: construction parts FIRST (the eternal early bottleneck), then mechanical parts, then electronics (starter phase 2). Placement route (v1.2.2): authored as pack slug starter-assemblies-v1 — companion /place flow, human confirm, QoSBuilder job.

orders.step: Set one manual assembly to the Construction Parts I recipe and confirm it is producing; set a second to Mechanical Parts once construction parts flow.
orders.why: MachineToggleRecipeActiveCmd exists (verified) but needs a runtime machine id + exact recipe id, neither sourced for a fresh save; the recipe choice is the human's until entity resolution is exercised in sandbox. Agent may prepare the command form in-session once the assembly's entity id is known from census/topology.

orders.note: Maintenance depot online in this phase (starter phase 2). Temporary siting is acceptable — it moves with the districts later.
One farm near the settlement (starter phase 2). Crop assignment is manual: FarmAssignCropCmd exists (wired) but crop proto ids are not sourced in the starter material, so no crop id is written here.
Construction parts are the phase-spanning bottleneck; keep them pinned.

checks.note: One refugee wave is 16 pops. If free housing < 16 and the beacon is on, the next wave over-accepts past capacity and costs Unity (research-order.md / bottlenecks.md). Refugee acceptance itself has no catalogue command (format G9) — switching the beacon off is a manual step the human takes from this report.

Proxy only: 'trucks extremely busy' is a UI signal with no API equivalent. Zero iron-ore flow while the mine exists usually means logistics, not geology — scale the fleet, don't tune around it (bottlenecks.md).
Floor raised vs phase 2: the truck fleet is now a diesel consumer at scale. Plan-set target.

entry_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: Vehicles & Mining ends reliance on the scrap pile: coal mine first (retiring the coal maker smoothly), then iron mine + ore smelter anchoring the PERMANENT smelting district, truck fleet grown aggressively for the long iron haul.
phases.name: Mining & vehicles

orders.note: Research order #3. Display name in sources is 'Trading Dock' (U4-verified); the game id spells it TradeDock. The dock is the emergency bailout — it buys any shortage and prevents game-over. Placement note from the source: needs only -2 ocean depth since v0.8.1, much easier early placement.
Research order #4. Display name 'Vehicles & Mining' is U4-verified; the game id is singular 'Vehicle'. Unlocks vehicle depot, Mine Control Tower, Ore Sorting Plant (research-order.md).
Coal mine FIRST (starter phase 3), sited per the phase-0 scout. Keep mine edges well back from permanent processing — veins run below sea level and terrain collapses into pits (layout policy rule 3).

orders.step: Decommission the wood-burning coal maker SMOOTHLY, in this order: stop truck imports of wood to it, let it burn its remaining wood, and only then remove it — removal itself is a human in-UI act (deconstruction is banned for the agent in this plan).
orders.why: Starter phase 3 prescribes the smooth retirement sequence; the plan encodes the sequence, not a demolition order.

orders.note: Iron mine + ore-based smelter. The ore smelter ANCHORS the permanent smelting district — place thoughtfully in the reserved inland area, not in the starter cluster (layout policy). This is the phase's one permanent siting decision. Placement route (v1.2.2): the smelter anchor (pack slugs iron-v1 + overlay iron-v2) goes through the companion /place flow — human confirm, QoSBuilder job; the iron mine itself is deposit-sited and placed manually (plans-blueprint-status.md ref #6).

protoId.confirm: Vehicle proto ids are not in the starter material; source from the vehicle depot UI / game data before use.

orders.note: Grow the fleet aggressively for the iron haul (starter phase 3), but keep it lean — small vehicles are upgraded manually later (unassign → scrap → rebuild), so do not over-invest (bottlenecks.md). Wired command (not verified); the proto placeholder makes this order manual-only until sourced.
Research order #5 (U4-verified id). Refugee waves are 16 pops each — see the beacon check below; the beacon gets switched OFF before housing is exceeded.
Research order #6: the QoL suite (copy/cut, copy settings, Unity tool, pause tool, upgrade, planning mode) that makes every later build faster.

checks.note: Once the basic diesel chain exists, a negative monthly diesel balance is the earliest death-spiral warning — earlier than any stock floor. Diesel chain guard (Round 5): the lifetime-produced sibling in the when: all: means this can only fire once a diesel chain has actually produced diesel — before that, a negative balance is ordinary starting-stock drawdown, not a chain deficit.
Diesel done but zero rubber: the postponement trap bottlenecks.md names explicitly.

exit_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: The transitional industry phase: limestone mine + kiln for concrete, oil pumps + basic distiller + rubber maker at the oil patch. Rubber and copper cannot be postponed — this phase ends with a REAL diesel chain replacing the starting stock, and rubber flowing.
phases.name: Concrete, diesel & rubber

orders.note: Research order #7. Id SOURCED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): no node displays as 'Concrete Production' in the shipped data; the wiki Required Research trio for this step (Crusher, Rotary Kiln, Concrete Mixer) is the exact unlock list of the node registered as Start("Advanced concrete", Ids.Research.ConcreteAdvanced) in Mafi.Base (MiningAndSmeltingResearchData) — shipped display name 'Advanced concrete'. The v1.2.x caution against substituting ResearchConcreteAdvanced was based on its name alone and is superseded by the proto data; the string also appears in Philip's live bridge researched list.

Limestone mine + rotary kiln + concrete mixer (starter phase 4), using the phase-0 scout's limestone position. Transitional siting: concrete production will be rebuilt at scale later; do not overbuild it here. Placement route (v1.2.2): the kiln+mixer block (pack slug concrete-v1) goes through the companion /place flow — human confirm, QoSBuilder job; the limestone mine is deposit-sited and placed manually.

Research order #8. Id exists in research_ids.txt; the exact display form 'Basic Diesel' is single-source in research-tree.md (Charles says 'diesel'; Medium guide corroborates the progression) — flag carried.

At the oil patch (phase-0 scout): 3 oil pumps + basic distiller, wastewater dumped — layout policy explicitly calls this design 'not the most scalable' and temporary. Diesel generators stay on the output side of fuel storage (bottlenecks.md structural rule). Placement route (v1.2.2): the distiller block (pack slug diesel-v1) goes through the companion /place flow — human confirm, QoSBuilder job; the 3 pumps sit on oil-patch tiles and are placed manually (plans-blueprint-status.md ref #8).

Turn on the game's own storage alert for the diesel buffer, firing when the level falls BELOW its threshold (SPEC §12.7: align with native alerts rather than duplicating them). Arg names verified against live/commands.json 2026-11-02 (storageId / isEnabled / isAbove). StorageAlertSetThresholdCmd (wired) may set the level in-session.

Research order #9. 'Cannot be postponed: no rubber, no vehicles/electronics, no maintenance, no death spiral' (research-order.md). Id SOURCED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): shipped proto registration Start("Synthetic rubber", Ids.Research.RubberProduction) in Mafi.Base (RefineryResearchData; unlocks VacuumDistillationTower + the diesel/coal rubber recipe); of the two old candidates, ResearchRubberProduction is the node and ResearchRubber is not registered as one. The string appears in Philip's live bridge researched list.
Rubber maker next to the basic diesel chain (starter phase 4). Placement route (v1.2.2): pack slug rubber-v1 — companion /place flow, human confirm, QoSBuilder job.

checks.note: The ship's copper stock is finite (layout policy). Low copper + no copper-ore flow = the copper district is late. Threshold is a plan-set target.
Stricter than the global floor: this phase's whole point is food security, so it reports earlier.
No power route exists (format G2): electrolysis + a 3rd generator change the power balance, and a rising starved share is the available proxy. Do not gate on MW — there is no MW source.

entry_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

exit_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: Spend the ship's copper wisely while the permanent copper district (mine + smelter + electrolysis, near power — it is thirsty for water and power) comes online BEFORE the ship stock runs out. Construction II unlocks electric assemblies and the permanent conveyor-ready assembly area. Food security is gated explicitly here: the farm base must carry the settlement with margin.
phases.name: Copper, Construction II & food security

orders.note: Research order #10 (U4-verified display name + exact id in research_ids.txt). Note: a separate ResearchCopper id also exists in the game data — if the research screen shows it as a prerequisite, queue it first (human confirms while queueing; the plan does not guess the prerequisite graph, which research-tree.md says is not publicly documented).

PERMANENT build (layout policy): copper mine + smelter + electrolysis, sited near the power district because electrolysis is thirsty for water and power. Likely needs a 3rd diesel generator (starter phase 5) — adding it is part of this build step, on the output side of fuel storage.

Research order #11: electric assemblies (2x manual speed) + yellow construction parts; gateway to automation. Id SOURCED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): shipped proto registration Start("Construction II", Ids.Research.Cp2Packing) in Mafi.Base (ConstructionResearchData; unlocks AssemblyElectrified + Cp2Assembly recipe) — the Cp2 = Construction Parts II reading was right, but the full node id is ResearchCp2Packing, confirmed in Philip's live bridge researched list.

Start the PERMANENT conveyor-ready assembly area with storage buffers (starter phase 5). As it comes online, begin retiring disposable starter buildings — retirement means pause/stop first; any actual removal is a human act (deconstruction banned for the agent).

orders.step: Expand farming beyond the phase-2 single farm until the food buffer is visibly growing: additional farms near the settlement, crops assigned in the farm UI (crop proto ids unsourced — no FarmAssignCropCmd order is written in this plan). Keep food variety simple at this stage; the gate below (monthsOfFood) is the arbiter, not farm count.
orders.why: The starter skill seeds one farm in phase 2 and treats food as a settlement commitment (refugees/housing); this plan makes food security an explicit gated phase outcome using the bridge status route, which is the only honest food metric available.

checks.note: Belt conversion leaves dangling transports; the census transports block (total vs fullyConnected) is the observable. Threshold is a plan-set target.

exit_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: Conveyor Belts kill the truck chaos: electric assemblies, belt-fed lines, unit storages with keep-full import rules — one dedicated line per product, no sushi belts. Ship repaired, groundwater and fuel station round out the first-15. Districts from the layout policy become the map's permanent shape.
phases.name: Automation & expansion districts

orders.note: Research order #12 (U4-verified display name; exact id in research_ids.txt). Flag: a ResearchConveyors id also exists — if the screen shows Conveyors as the belt-unlocking node instead, amend the plan rather than guessing.

orders.step: Belt-feed the permanent assembly district: one dedicated line per product, no sushi belts, no permanent multi-recipe factories (starter phase 6). Unit storages get keep-full import rules — set them in the storage UI; the agent may prepare StorageSetSliderStepCmd (wired) per storage in-session once the storage entity id is resolved from the bridge storages route, but slider VALUES are not readable back (format G7), so verify is human-confirm.
orders.why: Belts are placement (format G3) and sliders are write-only state (G7); both stay human-led in v1 of this plan.

orders.note: Research order #13. Id CORRECTED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): this order previously named ResearchShipDockRepair, which is a GOAL id (GoalsData: GoalToResearchNode "ResearchShipDockRepair" targets Ids.Research.RepairDock) and would have failed at prepare. The node is ResearchRepairDock — shipped registration Start("Ship dock repair", Ids.Research.RepairDock) in Mafi.Base (ConstructionResearchData; unlocks the Shipyard2 layout entity), confirmed in Philip's live bridge researched list. The old note's conflation warning had the relationship backwards and is retired.

orders.step: Repair the capital ship at the shipyard and begin world-map exploration (offshore oil is the phase-7 prize). Shipyard commands exist (wired) but repair flow semantics are untested; the human drives this in the UI.
orders.why: Starter phase 7 opens with ship repair → world map → offshore oil.

orders.note: Research order #14. Id SOURCED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0): shipped proto registration Start("Groundwater pump", Ids.Research.UndergroundWater) in Mafi.Base — the plan's inferred candidate was the right node; the string appears in Philip's live bridge researched list. Scalable water replaces rainwater collectors.
Research order #15 (U4-verified display name + exact id). Vehicle refuelling logistics — the truck fleet's diesel stops being hand-carried.
First fuel station near the vehicle depot / docks (vehicle depot siting is permanent per layout policy: near the docks).

orders.observe: Record for the NEXT plan (do not queue blindly): after the first 15, the source order is Advanced Diesel (id ResearchAdvancedDiesel exists) → Power Generation (coal boiler + steam turbine replacing diesel generators; candidate ids ResearchPowerGeneration2 / ResearchPowerGen2 are ambiguous — unsourced mapping) → Cargo Depot (id ResearchCargoDepot exists; explicit gate per a single-source community report: it cannot be researched until a cargo ship is discovered).

checks.note: If converting the iron haul to rail makes iron flow WORSE, the shuttle is wrong (blocked/mis-scheduled), not the plan — report with the trains route evidence.

entry_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

exit_gate.note: Vacuous-window guard (Round 5): the activity sibling (produced or consumed > 0 in the same window) prevents this net_flow leaf reading TRUE on 0-0 when the window never existed or the product had no activity in it.

phases.intent: First rail, honestly scoped: the starter skill hands rail off to the coi-trains sibling skill and notes the in-game train tutorials are new in Update 4 — use them. This phase stands up ONE network and ONE line on the longest truck haul (iron), built by hand, with the command-channel train primitives kept sandbox-only until their semantics are validated (format G3/G10).
phases.name: Rail introduction (Trains Expansion DLC)

orders.note: DLC gate node. Id exists in research_ids.txt; display name 'Trains' is single-source in research-tree.md (DLC section). A ResearchTrains2 id also exists (later tier — not this phase). Diesel locomotives are a separate later node family (ResearchDieselLocomotiveT2 is T2; the base diesel-loco node id is NOT sourced here and is not guessed).

orders.step: Complete the in-game train tutorials (new in Update 4) before laying any track.
orders.why: Starter phase 7's explicit instruction: 'In-game train tutorials are new in Update 4 — use them.' Detailed rail design belongs to the coi-trains sibling skill, not this plan.

orders.step: Lay the first line by hand in the UI: a dedicated iron-ore shuttle, mine → smelting district, stations on sidings (never blocking a through route), load-only station at the mine and unload-only station at the smelter (a station cannot load and unload the same product — the relocation plan's station spec, applied here as doctrine), buffer storage >= 1 trainload at each end, fuel station on the route. Detailed consists and network rules come from the coi-trains skill.
orders.why: Track/station placement semantics via CreateTrainTrackEntityWithDirectionCmd are untested (format G3/G10); manual laying is the honest v1 path.

orders.note: Catalogue command (wired, no args). Recorded here so the plan names the real primitive — but it MUST NOT be applied to this run until sandbox validation is recorded (format §6.1). The in-UI equivalent in p7-build-first-line-manual is the v1 path.
Same status as the network command: real catalogue primitive, wired, untested semantics. Sandbox-only in v1.

assumptions.claim: Starting area contains an abandoned comms station with free scrap iron and reportedly ~600 concrete slabs; oil patch NE of the start, coal nearby, limestone fairly close, iron a fair distance away, coast/docks to the south.
assumptions.source: layout-policy.md — reported hypothesis, NOT confirmed tile-level truth

assumptions.claim: Starting settlement is ~100 population against ~160 housing capacity in shipping containers; refugees arrive in waves of 16.
The starting ship's hold carries several hundred units of copper, covering early electronics until copper refining is online.
A fresh game starts with some diesel stock (vehicles and the first diesel generator run before any diesel chain exists), so the diesel invariant in globals can be armed from t0.
assumptions.confirm: Phase 0 scout verifies Product_Diesel quantity > 0; if it is 0, a human amends globals.invariants before the game is unpaused.
assumptions.source: inferred from starter phase 1 (diesel generator is a phase-1 build)

assumptions.claim: Research display names in the starter skill map to game node ids as recorded per-order in the phases below; mappings not marked 'sourced-id' are candidates or placeholders.
assumptions.source: research-order.md + research-tree.md (display-name verification) cross-checked against coi/data/research_ids.txt (extracted game ids)

assumptions.claim: The phase-2 entry research node (display name 'Construction') is ResearchCpPacking — RETIRED 2026-11-06 (plan v1.3.0) from the shipped game's proto registrations (Mafi.Base.dll, ConstructionResearchData: Start("Construction", Ids.Research.CpPacking) with this plan's exact unlock list), cross-checked against Philip's live bridge /research capture, whose researched list contains the string ResearchCpPacking. The 2026-11-03 investigation's sole candidate ResearchCp1Production is a GOAL id, not a research node (GoalsData: GoalToResearchNode "ResearchCp1Production" targets CpPacking) — the mixed id dump behind coi/data/research_ids.txt contains goal ids, which is why no id-to-name source seemed to exist. Sibling retirements in the same pass: Construction II = ResearchCp2Packing, Synthetic Rubber = ResearchRubberProduction, 'Concrete Production' = ResearchConcreteAdvanced (shipped display 'Advanced concrete').
assumptions.source: Mafi.Base.dll decompiled 2026-11-06 (Mafi.Base.Prototypes.Research/ConstructionResearchData.cs, RefineryResearchData.cs, MiningAndSmeltingResearchData.cs; Mafi.Base.Prototypes.Messages/GoalsData.cs); live-check/current/bridge-research.json (researched list)

assumptions.claim: Blueprint placement mechanism (v1.2.2): a place-blueprint order with asset_status: authored and a pack_slug is placed through the companion /place flow — the layout ships inside the companion's embedded library (tools/gen_blueprint_library.py, decode-verified at generation); Philip prepares and confirms in the website; only the confirm writes a single-use, expiring, gameId-pinned QoSBuilder job file; the mod places the layout as ordinary construction sites in one batch; the placement verdict is the companion's before/after census diff, and the order's own completion (human-confirm or verify predicates) is unchanged. Refs with asset_status: not-yet-authored have no library asset and still degrade to manual builds. The pack's strings are NOT in-game tested (library testing_status), so the first placement on the new save happens only under Philip's in-the-moment confirm.
assumptions.source: SPEC Addendum XVII (QoSBuilder job-file contract); coi/data/blueprint-library.json (82 entries; all six fresh-start pack_slugs present: iron-v1, iron-v2, starter-assemblies-v1, concrete-v1, diesel-v1, rubber-v1)

assumptions.claim: Update 4.3 (0.8.8) mechanics deltas relevant to this plan: mixed-materials support (storages/cargo buffers may hold mixed contents — the bridge storages route already reports mixed contents), info overlays, radiation-shielded trains, train stats, and the in-game web API. No recipe ratio changed. None of these alters an early-game phase, gate or order in this plan (full reasoning in the v1.2.2 changelog entry).
assumptions.source: 0.8.8 changelog via patch watch 2026-11-02 (coigame.com/Changelog); SPEC §3 storages route note

changelog.change: Research placeholder ids RETIRED from a primary source: the shipped game's own proto registrations (Mafi.Base.dll, Mafi.Base.Prototypes.Research — decompiled 2026-11-06), cross-checked against the bridge /research capture from Philip's live game (live-check/current/bridge-research.json), whose researched list carries the exact id strings. (1) 'Construction' = ResearchCpPacking — ConstructionResearchData registers Start("Construction", Ids.Research.CpPacking) unlocking AssemblyManual + the CpAssembly / MechPartsIronAssembly / ElectronicsAssembly recipes, exactly this plan's unlock list. The old sole candidate ResearchCp1Production is NOT a research node at all: it is a GOAL id (GoalsData: GoalToResearchNode "ResearchCp1Production" targets CpPacking), which is why it sat among the earliest goal strings and in the mixed id dump behind coi/data/research_ids.txt.
